literal: Lie had secretly learned of the plot, feared disaster for his house, and with his elder cousin Dun, governor of Guangping, galloped to Luoyang to report the danger.
idiomatic: Lie had already seen through the scheme. Dreading ruin for his clan, he and his elder cousin Dun, governor of Guangping, raced to Luoyang to raise the alarm.

literal: The court was about to heap rewards on him. Lie told others, "It is like cutting off the hand to save the body—what is preserved is the greater part. How could one take profit from a cousin's fall?"
idiomatic: The court meant to heap rewards on him. Lie told others, "It is like cutting off a hand to save the body—what remains is the greater part. How could I profit from a cousin's fall?"

literal: In the end he accepted nothing.
idiomatic: In the end he took nothing.

literal: At weak cap he was summoned as the province's chief clerk and also concurrently served as supervisory aide.
idiomatic: At weak cap the province summoned him as chief clerk; he also served concurrently as supervisory aide.

literal: The prefect cared only for clerical affairs; Lie was known for practical efficiency.
idiomatic: The prefect cared only for paperwork; Lie won notice for getting things done.

literal: He doffed the headcloth and became a staff officer under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Xing, then was promoted to secretariat gentleman.
idiomatic: He left private life for a staff post under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Xing, then rose to secretariat gentleman.

literal: At the start of Xianzu's reign he was grain-supply staff officer in an establishment of the third rank that opened the government.
idiomatic: When Xianzu came to power he was grain-supply staff officer in a third-rank opening office.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he was made Colonel of the Foot Soldiers for the Heir Apparent and General of the Light Chariots, soon moved to merged-bureau director in the revenue section, made attendant of the Secretariat, and passed through director of temple observances and director in the left and right people sections—wherever he served he was called competent.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was colonel of foot soldiers for the heir apparent and general of the light chariots, soon moved to merged-bureau director in the revenue section, then attendant of the Secretariat, and on through director of temple observances and the left and right people sections—every post he held earned the same verdict: competent.

literal: In the ninth year he was made governor of Yangping; his administration won a name for ability.
idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made governor of Yangping, and his rule won a name for ability.

literal: At that time locust plagues came often; they did not cross the border into Yangping, and an edict praised him.
idiomatic: Locusts ravaged the land year after year, yet their teeth never crossed into Yangping; an edict praised him for it.

literal: In the second year of Huangjian he was moved to vice director of the Imperial Household, given additional rank as General of the Dragon Cavalry and grand rectifier of Yan province, and further advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: In Huangjian's second year he was moved to vice director of the imperial household, given the dragon cavalry general's rank and the grand rectifier's post in Yan province, then advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: In the Tiantong era he was made grand master of splendid happiness and concurrently vice director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: In Tiantong he was made grand master of splendid happiness while keeping the vice directorship of the imperial household.

literal: At the start of Wuping he was made General of the Valiant Cavalry and governor of Yi province; soon, on account of age and illness, he returned home.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuping he was made general of the valiant cavalry and governor of Yi province; before long age and illness sent him home.

literal: In the Zhou Elephant era he died.
idiomatic: He died in the Zhou Elephant reign.

literal: The Lie household had long transmitted its proper craft; inner gates were kept in order, and the age praised them.
idiomatic: The Lie line had long kept its proper craft; their inner gates were kept in order, and the age praised them for it.

literal: In one household no woman married twice.
idiomatic: In that household no widow ever married again.

literal: In the Wei Taihe era they built a nunnery in Yan province; women who were widowed and childless all took the tonsure as nuns and kept the precepts.
idiomatic: In Wei Taihe they built a nunnery in Yan province; widows without sons all took the tonsure and kept the precepts.

literal: In Tiantong Lie disputed with Minister of the Masters of Writing Bi Yiyun over the grand rectifier's post in Yan province. Yiyun loudly vaunted his gate and house, saying, "For generations my family were governors of this province; your line were always our household clerks."
idiomatic: In Tiantong Lie quarreled with Minister of the Masters of Writing Bi Yiyun over the Yan grand rectifier's post. Yiyun boasted of his gate and house: "For generations we were governors here; your people were always clerks in our household."

literal: Lie answered, "Since your Bi Gui was executed, your line has been empty of men worth naming. The recent governors were all men who won their posts on the frontier, each snatching the other by turns—what is there to boast of?"
idiomatic: Lie answered, "Since your Bi Gui was executed, your line has been empty of anyone worth naming. The recent governors were all frontier men who seized the post by turns—what is there to boast of?"

literal: How can that compare with our Han Governor of Henan and our Jin Grand Tutor—name, virtue, learning, and conduct handed down in beauty for a hundred generations?
idiomatic: How does that compare with our Han Governor of Henan and our Jin Grand Tutor—name, virtue, learning, and conduct handed down in beauty for a hundred generations?

literal: Moreover our men are pure and our women chaste—enough to crown the rest; beyond that there is much else to praise.
idiomatic: Our men are pure and our women chaste—enough to crown the rest; beyond that there is much else to praise.

literal: This was meant to mock Yiyun's lax curtains.
idiomatic: He meant it as a jab at the lax curtains in Yiyun's household.

literal: Zhi's son Shen was Wei secretariat director.
idiomatic: Zhi's son Shen was Wei secretariat director.

literal: Shen's son Su was known for scholarship and cultivation; he was eastern-pavilion libationer in the heir apparent's great general's establishment.
idiomatic: Shen's son Su was known for scholarship; he was eastern-pavilion libationer in the great general's establishment of the heir apparent.

literal: At the start of Qianming he was supervisory aide of Ji province.
idiomatic: At the start of Qianming he was supervisory aide of Ji province.

literal: The Prince of Zhao commandery went out as touring inspection envoy; Su was dismissed for slowness and unfitness for office, but court opinion held him guiltless and he was soon restored.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao commandery toured as inspection envoy, Su was dismissed for slowness and unfitness; court opinion held him guiltless, and he was soon restored.

literal: At the start of Tiantong he was moved to chief aide of Southern Yan province.
idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was moved to chief aide of Southern Yan province.

literal: In Wuping he entered the Wenslin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.
idiomatic: In Wuping he entered the Wenslin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.

literal: Lie's younger brother Xiu had talent and capacity; in Daning he died as left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Lie's younger brother Xiu had talent and drive; in Daning he died as left vice director in the Masters of Writing.

literal: His son Xuanzheng, at the end of Wuping, was director of palace construction.
idiomatic: His son Xuanzheng, at the end of Wuping, was director of palace construction.

literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was vice minister of the people.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was vice minister of the people.

literal: He died as overseer of Longxi commandery.
idiomatic: He died while serving as overseer of Longxi commandery.

literal: Yuan Biao, styled Wenzong, was a man of Ledu in Xiping.
idiomatic: Yuan Biao, styled Wenzong, came from Ledu in Xiping.

literal: His father Zigong was Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke of Literature.
idiomatic: His father Zigong had been Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke of Literature.

literal: Wenzong was learned, alert, and quick-witted; from youth he had a name for ability.
idiomatic: Wenzong was learned, alert, and quick-witted; from youth he had a name for ability.

literal: In the Yong'an era of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei, for his father's merit he was given the barony of Linying and made irregular-attendant cavalier attendant.
idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's Yong'an era, for his father's merit he was given the barony of Linying and made irregular-attendant cavalier attendant.

literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he was grand rectifier of Liang province.
idiomatic: In Tianping's fourth year he was grand rectifier of Liang province.

literal: On his father's death he left office.
idiomatic: When his father died he left office.

literal: At the start of Wuding, when mourning ended, the Ministry of State Affairs summoned him to head the secretariat records office, with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuding, when mourning ended, the Ministry summoned him to head the secretariat records office and gave him the additional rank General Who Pacifies the East.

literal: When the heir apparent took charge of selection, terrace gentlemen were winnowed; Wenzong was made director of temple observances in the Masters of Writing while still heading the records office.
idiomatic: When the heir apparent took charge of selection and terrace gentlemen were winnowed, Wenzong was made director of temple observances while still heading the records office.

literal: He was moved to groom of the heir apparent.
idiomatic: He was moved to groom of the heir apparent.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was made heir-apparent palace aide.
idiomatic: In Tianbao's first year he was made heir-apparent palace aide.

literal: At the start of Qianming he went out as governor of Fanyang commandery.
idiomatic: At the start of Qianming he went out as governor of Fanyang commandery.

literal: In the second year of Huangjian he was made governor of Jing province.
idiomatic: In Huangjian's second year he was made governor of Jing province.

literal: Wenzong treated people with favor and trust and won great harmony on the frontier; neighbors admired him, and many whom earlier administrations had carried off in raids he secured and sent home.
idiomatic: Wenzong treated people with favor and trust and won deep harmony on the frontier; neighbors admired him, and many captives taken under earlier rule he secured and sent home.

literal: At the start of Tiantong he entered court as director in the civil service section, was moved to imperial censor, and still oversaw selection as before.
idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he entered court as director in the civil service section, then imperial censor, still overseeing selection as before.

literal: Soon he was made regular-attendant cavalier attendant while still acting in the civil service section, with additional rank as General of the Valiant Cavalry.
idiomatic: Soon he was regular-attendant cavalier attendant while still running the civil service section, with the additional rank general of the valiant cavalry.

literal: When Qin province's governor Song Song died, the court held that the province lay on the frontier; because Wenzong's tenure at Jing had won a strong reputation, he was made governor of Qin, traveled by post relay to the prefectural seat, and was specially granted rear escort music.
idiomatic: When Song Song, governor of Qin, died, the court judged the province a frontier post; Wenzong's record at Jing had been strong, so he was made governor of Qin, rode post relay to the seat, and was specially granted rear escort music.

literal: Wenzong governed as he had at Jing.
idiomatic: Wenzong governed Qin as he had governed Jing.

literal: Li Xiaozhen was sent on a mission to Chen; the Chen ruler told Xiaozhen, "Qi has again sent Governor Yuan of Jing to Guabu—truly this is harmony in full."
idiomatic: Li Xiaozhen went on embassy to Chen; the Chen ruler told him, "Qi has again sent Governor Yuan of Jing to Guabu—surely that is harmony in full."

literal: Soon he was given additional rank as establishment of the third rank.
idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional rank establishment of the third rank.

literal: In the second year of Wuping he was summoned to head the Directorate of the Sons of the State.
idiomatic: In Wuping's second year he was summoned to head the Directorate of the Sons of the State.

literal: In the third year he was moved to secretariat supervisor.
idiomatic: In the third year he was moved to secretariat supervisor.

literal: Chen's general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell in succession.
idiomatic: Chen's general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell one after another.

literal: Zhao Yanshen, in private at the Office for Imperial Progress, secretly asked Wenzong, "Wu the bandit swells and has come to this. I have long blocked the worthy and am torn by worry and fear. In today's situation, what plan will do?"
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen, in private at the Office for Imperial Progress, asked Wenzong, "Wu the bandit swells and has come to this. I have long stood in the way of better men and live in worry and fear. What plan will serve today's situation?"

literal: When you were at Jing you knew the Huai and Jiang country well—how will you defend against them now?"
idiomatic: You once governed Jing and know the Huai and Jiang country well—how will you defend against them now?"

literal: He answered, "I owe the state deep favor and have no way to repay it; what I have seen and heard I dare not hold back."
idiomatic: He answered, "I owe the state deep favor and have no way to repay it; what I have seen and heard I dare not hold back."

literal: But the court's crack troops will surely not be given in large numbers to the generals; a few thousand at most cannot contend with Wu and Chu. Sending generals out will only feed the enemy.
idiomatic: But the court will never give its crack troops in large numbers to field commanders; a few thousand at most cannot stand against Wu and Chu. To send generals out is only to feed the enemy.

literal: Wei Pohu's character Your Majesty already knows.
idiomatic: Your Majesty already knows Wei Pohu's character.

literal: Advance he cannot achieve; retreat he cannot take; defeat is not a matter of mornings and evenings.
idiomatic: He cannot advance with success; he cannot retreat in safety; defeat is not a matter of mornings and evenings.

literal: If Your Majesty goes out and can come in again, court and country will lean on you; if one day things go awry, regret will have no place to stand.
idiomatic: If Your Majesty goes out and can come in again, court and country will lean on you; if one day things go awry, there will be no place left for regret.

literal: On today's plan there must be no third try.
idiomatic: On today's plan there must be no third try.

literal: The state's treatment of Huainan has failed it like a mere arrow of wormwood.
idiomatic: The state's treatment of Huainan has failed it like a mere arrow of wormwood.

literal: By Wenzong's reckoning nothing surpasses entrusting Wang Lin alone: recruit thirty or forty thousand men in Huainan—customs match, they will fight to the death—and let him also command the old officers' north-of-the-Huai draft troops; that is enough to hold firm.
idiomatic: By Wenzong's reckoning nothing surpasses putting everything in Wang Lin's hands: recruit thirty or forty thousand men in Huainan—customs match, they will fight to the death—and let him also command the old officers' north-of-the-Huai draft troops; that is enough to hold firm.

literal: Moreover Lin toward Xuandi of Chen plainly will not bow north and serve him—this, I venture, is the plan above all plans.
idiomatic: Moreover Lin toward Chen's Xuandi plainly will not bow north and serve him—I venture this is the plan above all plans.

literal: If you do not give Lin your open heart but send others to check him, you will again bring swift disaster—still less can that be done.
idiomatic: If you do not give Lin your open heart but send others to check him, you will again bring swift disaster—still less can that be done.

literal: Yanshen sighed and said, "Brother, this fine plan would win a thousand li away—but the tongue has argued for ten days already and no one will follow it."
idiomatic: Yanshen sighed and said, "Brother, this fine plan would win a thousand li away—but tongues have argued for ten days already and no one will follow it."

literal: The times have come to this—how can everything be spoken!"
idiomatic: The times have come to this—how can everything be spoken!"

literal: Thereupon they looked at each other and wept.
idiomatic: Thereupon they looked at each other and wept.

literal: In the seventh year of Wuping, when Zhou pacified Qi, together with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Yuxiu, and eighteen others he was edicted into the capital, made General of the Establishment of the Same Rank and junior mentor in the Directorate of the Sons of the State.
idiomatic: In Wuping's seventh year, when Zhou pacified Qi, he was edicted into the capital with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Yuxiu, and eighteen others, and made general of the establishment of the same rank and junior mentor in the Directorate of the Sons of the State.

literal: At the start of Sui Kaihuang he was made governor of Ju province; on reaching the province he fell ill and left office.
idiomatic: At the start of Sui Kaihuang he was made governor of Ju province; on reaching the province he fell ill and left office.

literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang he died, aged sixty-six.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang's sixth year he died, at sixty-six.

literal: Wenzong, as a young man of noble houses who rose in the court ranks, was quick in talent and insight and known for practical capacity.
idiomatic: Wenzong rose through the court ranks as a young man of noble houses, quick in talent and insight and known for practical capacity.

literal: Yet he loved to visit the gates of the powerful and influential, so opinion of the time held that he was skilled at currying favor.
idiomatic: Yet he loved to visit the gates of the powerful, so opinion of the time held that he was skilled at currying favor.

literal: His son Shi from youth loved learning, was clear in judgment and keen in understanding, and was especially known for clerical affairs.
idiomatic: His son Shi from youth loved learning, was clear in judgment and keen in understanding, and was especially known for clerical affairs.

literal: At the start of Heqing he was staff officer in the Ministry of Works, and passed through attendant censor, director in the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, and director in the left outer military section of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the start of Heqing he was staff officer in the Ministry of Works, then passed through attendant censor, director in the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, and director in the left outer military section.

literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was director in the revenue section and vice director of merit assessment.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was director in the revenue section and vice director of merit assessment.

literal: Early in Daye he died as vice minister of justice.
idiomatic: Early in Daye he died as vice minister of justice.

literal: Wenzong's younger brother Wenzju also had talent and capacity; he passed through director in the revenue section, director of the two-thousand-bushel section, and chief aide of Ding province while concurrently governing Zhongshan commandery.
idiomatic: Wenzong's younger brother Wenju also had talent and capacity; he passed through director in the revenue section, director of the two-thousand-bushel section, and chief aide of Ding province while concurrently governing Zhongshan commandery.

literal: He died as chief aide of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He died as chief aide of the Grand Commandant.

literal: Wenzong's elder cousin by the father's line Kai, styled Nayian, had capacity and drive and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
idiomatic: Wenzong's elder cousin Kai, styled Nayian, had capacity and drive and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

literal: He passed through director in the left people section of the Masters of Writing, investigating censor, governor of Changle and Zhongshan commanderies, metropolitan chief aide, gate gentleman, and acting establishment of the third rank.
idiomatic: He passed through director in the left people section, investigating censor, governor of Changle and Zhongshan, metropolitan chief aide, gate gentleman, and acting establishment of the third rank.

literal: When Qi fell, eminent men of the court known by name who entered the Zhou capital included Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Revenue, a descendant of Emperor Wencheng of Wei—pure, sparing in desire, clear in grasp of principle and form.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, eminent men known by name who entered the Zhou capital included Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Revenue, a descendant of Emperor Wencheng of Wei—pure, sparing in desire, clear in grasp of principle and form.

literal: From youth he passed through eminent posts—gentleman in the Masters of Writing, investigating censor, left chief aide of the Secretariat, several commandery governors, and governor of Guang province—and wherever he served won a name for achievement.
idiomatic: From youth he passed through eminent posts—gentleman in the Masters of Writing, investigating censor, left chief aide of the Secretariat, several commandery governorships, and governor of Guang—and wherever he served won a name for achievement.

literal: When he became Minister of Revenue, government was wasteful and the state narrow; storehouses were empty and levies and corvée multiplied.
idiomatic: When he became Minister of Revenue, government was wasteful and the state narrow; storehouses stood empty and levies and corvée multiplied.

literal: Xiubo grieved for the state as for his own house, pitied the people's labor, and together aided the affairs of the time; he sought counsel from the chancellor morning and evening with tireless zeal, and with Recorder of the Masters of Writing Tang Yong exchanged views on what to take and what to leave—quite to the good.
idiomatic: Xiubo grieved for the state as for his own house, pitied the people's labor, and together aided the affairs of the time; morning and evening he sought counsel from the chancellor with tireless zeal, and with Recorder Tang Yong exchanged views on what to take and what to leave—quite to the good.

literal: The Zhou court made him General of the Establishment of the Same Rank and Master of the Carriage Office.
idiomatic: The Zhou court made him general of the establishment of the same rank and master of the carriage office.

literal: His deeds are missing from the histories, so he is not listed in a biography.
idiomatic: His deeds are missing from the histories, so he is not given a biography here.

literal: At the end of Qi there were also Xin Ti of Longxi, director in the merged-bureau Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
idiomatic: At the end of Qi there were also Xin Ti of Longxi, merged-bureau director in the Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.

literal: They entered service under Zhou and Sui and rose to eminent posts, it is said.
idiomatic: They entered service under Zhou and Sui and rose to eminent posts, it is said.

literal: The historiographer says: Li Zhilian and the others, by talent and capacity, won fame wherever they served.
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Zhilian and the others, by talent and capacity, won fame wherever they served.

literal: Feng Shu amassed wealth and was worn down by stinginess; Jiliang was held back by shallow learning; Wenzong was praised for currying favor.
idiomatic: Feng Shu amassed wealth and was worn down by stinginess; Xu Dun, styled Jiliang, was held back by shallow learning; Wenzong was praised for currying favor.

literal: Yet the two worthies Yang and Li were complete in virtue—gentlemen, should they not take care!
idiomatic: Yet the two worthies Yang and Li were complete in virtue—gentlemen, should they not take care!

literal: Praise: Only these several worthies—work steadfast and firm.
idiomatic: Praise: Only these several worthies—work steadfast and firm.

literal: In life touched by censure, in death preserved in silk.
idiomatic: In life touched by censure, in death preserved in silk.

literal: Feng and Yuan, Xu—ended as worms in their own flesh.
idiomatic: Feng and Yuan, Xu—ended as worms in their own flesh.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
